course: Course is VERY OUTDATED. This is not something I would expect from CTIS, as they always claim to be up-to-date with emerging technologies. However, I think this does not apply when it comes to CTIS255 and CTIS256 courses. I had many discussions with instructors regarding this topic, as I believe it doesn't make sense to teach jQuery + PHP at the year of 2022. They argue that it would not be possible to teach React + NodeJS in 14 lecture weeks, however I believe that even teaching vanilla JS + TypeScript + NodeJS would be easily doable and much better compared to outdated jQuery + PHP stack. While my instructors have argued that "jQuery is currently dominant on web technologies when we take a look at top 1 million websites' web framework", that sadly doesn't necessarily mean it's the most favored framework of the time. Even though it may seem like around 98% of the websites in top 1 million ranking have jQuery in their client, this doesn't necessarily mean they built their whole web page based on jQuery, but rather it is just most likely due to legacy code that doesn't make sense to refactor and update to new technologies, as they are working fine as is so no point of making any changes on a thing that's running fine. However, when we look at the statistics of the web framework that is used most popular when building a new website from scratch, we see that React + NodeJS outnumbers jQuery by factors. I hope in the future that even though they may not switch to React, at least they would switch to vanilla JS since as of now, it can perform almost everything jQuery can do so no need to teach outdated frameworks/libraries such as that in my opinion.
